headline: High: shared MCP/networked workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict risks; B can also cascade A's CRM outputs into downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use direct function calls or an MCP server, and next-ai-draw-io uses MCP plus natural-language commands. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if A’s outputs are fed into B or a shared MCP channel, even though no direct pairwise integration is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A’s output is copied into B’s prompt or MCP context
IF both agents share the same MCP server without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable shared MCP routing between the agents
Add a prompt firewall that strips instructions from A’s text outputs
Require explicit human review before B consumes A-generated content
Use separate workspaces or tenants for each agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and handle sensitive classes: A touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data; B processes PDFs, text, and images while calling third-party model APIs. If A’s data is passed into B for document processing, leakage to external inference providers is plausible in default configurations. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A forwards CRM/email/calendar content into B
IF B sends those documents to a third-party model endpoint
mitigations: Block sensitive fields before handing data from A to B
Route B to a local-only model for sensitive documents
Separate credentials and tenants for each agent
Turn off external API providers in B for protected data

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad networked integrations; A writes through APIs like Google Sheets, Slack, Notion, email, and CRM, while B can use MCP and multiple model backends. Overlapping mutable surfaces make write conflicts plausible, but the profiles do not prove a shared writable directory or shared OAuth scopes, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same CRM, sheet, or workspace
IF no external locking or lease mechanism is configured
mitigations: Assign disjoint resources to each agent
Enable per-resource locking or leases
Restrict one agent to read-only access
Schedule writes in non-overlapping windows

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a sales-CRM agent that can generate research, email, and CRM content; B is a document-processing agent that can turn inputs into visual outputs and uses natural-language commands. If B treats A’s generated text or facts as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream documents or actions. Because the profiles show no verification barrier, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated summaries or facts without verification
IF B renders or acts on those outputs in user-facing artifacts
mitigations: Require source citations before B accepts A outputs
Add a verification step against original documents
Limit B to formatting only, not factual synthesis
Flag A-originated content as untrusted metadata

E_compliance.rationale: A touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data; B processes files and sends prompts to multiple external model providers. That combination creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch or third-party disclosure issue, but the profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so this is a medium compliance risk rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated or region-bound data from A is sent into B
IF B’s configured model provider retains prompts or files beyond policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B by default
Document retention settings for every provider B can call
Use region-appropriate providers only
Add a pre-send compliance checklist for A-to-B transfers
